title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Confidence Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Models via Selective Chain-of-Thought Triggering
description:
Problem: AutoVLA's adaptive reasoning selects between fast and slow thinking modes, but the triggering mechanism relies on learned heuristics that may fail silently in safety-critical edge cases (e.g., occlusions, adverse weather, novel scenarios). There is no principled uncertainty quantification to guide when deliberate reasoning is truly necessary versus when confident fast-path execution is safe.

Method: We propose augmenting the VLA framework with an epistemic uncertainty head trained via conformal prediction on trajectory token distributions. Rather than binary fast/slow mode selection, we introduce a continuous 'reasoning budget' proportional to predictive uncertainty. When uncertainty exceeds a calibrated threshold, the model is forced into slow thinking with structured safety-focused chain-of-thought prompting. We further introduce a safety-constrained GRPO variant where reward shaping penalizes overconfident fast-thinking in high-uncertainty scenarios, using collision proximity as an implicit uncertainty ground truth signal.

Experiments: (1) Uncertainty calibration quality (ECE, reliability diagrams) on nuScenes and Waymo OOD splits. (2) Closed-loop collision rate vs. reasoning frequency trade-off on CARLA in fog/rain conditions. (3) Ablation of threshold selection methods (fixed vs. adaptive conformal). (4) Comparison against AutoVLA baseline and vanilla temperature scaling, demonstrating improved safety without sacrificing throughput in routine scenarios.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Failure Prediction and Recovery in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models via Conformal Risk Calibration
description: Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates strong average-case planning performance, VLA models lack principled mechanisms to detect when their reasoning and trajectory predictions are unreliable, particularly in out-of-distribution scenarios. This creates safety risks in deployment since the model may confidently output physically plausible but contextually dangerous trajectories without triggering fallback behaviors. Proposed Method: We introduce SafeVLA, which augments a VLA backbone (based on AutoVLA's architecture) with a lightweight conformal prediction layer that estimates trajectory-level uncertainty at inference time. We exploit the internal token probability distributions of the autoregressive model to construct nonconformity scores calibrated on a held-out safety-critical scenario set. When uncertainty exceeds adaptive thresholds, the system switches to a conservative fallback policy (e.g., controlled deceleration) and triggers explicit slow-thinking reasoning to recover. We further propose a risk-sensitive GRPO variant that penalizes overconfident failures during reinforcement fine-tuning. Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA with injected distribution shifts (adverse weather, sensor degradation, novel obstacles), measuring (1) false negative rates for hazardous trajectory detection, (2) coverage guarantees from conformal bounds, (3) closed-loop collision rates with/without fallback activation, and (4) latency overhead versus baseline AutoVLA.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Safety Constraints for Vision-Language-Action Models via Conformal Prediction
description:
Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates strong planning performance, VLA models for autonomous driving lack formal safety guarantees — they can generate plausible-looking but unsafe trajectories, especially in rare or out-of-distribution scenarios. Existing reinforcement fine-tuning reward signals are heuristic and don't provide statistical safety bounds.

Proposed Method: We introduce SafeVLA, which augments VLA trajectory generation with conformal prediction-based uncertainty quantification to enforce formal safety certificates. At inference time, we construct prediction sets over tokenized trajectory distributions using a calibration dataset, computing coverage-guaranteed safety envelopes around planned trajectories. When the VLA's predicted trajectory falls outside safe conformal bounds (e.g., proximity to obstacles, velocity limits), we trigger a constrained re-sampling procedure that steers generation toward the safe prediction set. We additionally propose a safety-aware GRPO variant where the reward function explicitly penalizes trajectories violating conformal safety bounds, training the model to internalize these constraints.

Planned Experiments: (1) Safety violation rate comparison against AutoVLA baseline on nuPlan and CARLA closed-loop benchmarks; (2) Coverage guarantee verification under distribution shift (weather, lighting); (3) Ablation on conformal coverage levels (90%, 95%, 99%) vs. planning performance trade-off; (4) Evaluation of calibration efficiency with varying calibration set sizes; (5) Rare scenario stress tests using adversarial traffic agents in CARLA.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Scenario Augmentation for Robust Causal Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:
Problem: VLA driving models like AutoVLA learn correlational patterns from real-world demonstrations, making them brittle to distribution shifts and unable to distinguish causal factors (e.g., a pedestrian's intent) from spurious correlations (e.g., weather appearance). This limits safety-critical generalization without explicit causal structure.

Method: We propose CausalVLA, which augments VLA training with counterfactual scenario generation. Using a controllable diffusion-based scene editor, we systematically generate counterfactual variants of training scenes by intervening on specific causal variables (pedestrian trajectory, vehicle occlusion, traffic light state) while holding others fixed. We then train the VLA with a contrastive causal reasoning objective: the model must produce consistent action changes aligned with counterfactual interventions and explain which visual elements causally drove its decision in chain-of-thought outputs. A causal consistency reward is integrated into GRPO fine-tuning, penalizing action outputs that contradict counterfactual intervention logic.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes and CARLA with (1) standard benchmarks, (2) held-out distribution shift scenarios (novel weather/density), (3) adversarial interventions (removed traffic lights, occluded agents), and (4) a new CausalBench metric measuring action sensitivity to ground-truth causal variable changes. We compare against AutoVLA and data-augmentation baselines, expecting improved robustness and interpretability without sacrificing nominal performance.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Risk Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Models via Conformal Prediction
description: Problem: While AutoVLA and similar VLA models achieve competitive planning performance, they lack principled uncertainty quantification — they produce point-estimate trajectories without indicating when the model is operating outside its competence. This is safety-critical: a confident but wrong trajectory prediction in a novel scenario (construction zones, adverse weather, rare pedestrian behaviors) can cause accidents. Proposed Method: We introduce SafeVLA, which wraps a pretrained VLA model (e.g., AutoVLA) with conformal prediction to produce statistically guaranteed trajectory prediction sets. During calibration, we compute nonconformity scores between predicted and ground-truth trajectories across held-out scenarios, establishing per-scenario-type coverage bounds. At inference, SafeVLA outputs a minimal trajectory envelope (prediction region) with a user-specified coverage guarantee (e.g., 90%). When this envelope exceeds a safety threshold width, the system triggers fallback behaviors (deceleration, handoff). We additionally train a lightweight risk-aware meta-controller using the envelope width as a learned reward signal within the existing GRPO framework to proactively avoid high-uncertainty situations. Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan, nuScenes, and CARLA across distribution-shift scenarios (new cities, weather perturbations, adversarial agents), measuring coverage validity, envelope tightness, collision rates under fallback policies, and comparison against MC-Dropout and ensemble baselines.

title: SafeThink: Uncertainty-Aware Chain-of-Thought Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:
Problem: AutoVLA and similar VLA models adaptively reason but lack explicit uncertainty quantification in their chain-of-thought outputs. When a model confidently produces incorrect reasoning chains, downstream trajectory errors can be safety-critical. Current VLA models have no mechanism to express epistemic uncertainty about their own reasoning steps, making it difficult to know when to defer to fallback systems or request human intervention.

Proposed Method: We introduce SafeThink, which augments VLA reasoning with step-level uncertainty estimation. We fine-tune a driving VLA (based on AutoVLA's architecture) using a conformal prediction framework applied to intermediate reasoning tokens, assigning confidence scores to each reasoning step. We construct calibration sets from driving scenarios where ground-truth outcomes are known, fitting nonconformity scores at each chain-of-thought step. During inference, low-confidence reasoning steps trigger slow-thinking escalation or safe fallback maneuvers. We additionally train a lightweight uncertainty head alongside GRPO fine-tuning to jointly optimize trajectory quality and calibration error.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA closed-loop benchmarks measuring (1) collision rates conditioned on uncertainty thresholds, (2) Expected Calibration Error of reasoning steps, (3) intervention frequency vs. safety trade-off curves, and (4) ablations comparing conformal vs. dropout-based uncertainty. We demonstrate that uncertainty-aware reasoning reduces critical failures by selectively escalating complex scenarios while maintaining efficiency on routine driving.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Safety Verification for Vision-Language-Action Driving Models via Conformal Prediction
description:
Problem: While AutoVLA and similar VLA models generate feasible trajectories, they lack formal safety guarantees — the model may be confidently wrong in rare or out-of-distribution scenarios (adverse weather, novel obstacle configurations), posing deployment risks. Existing approaches either over-constrain the model or provide no coverage guarantees.

Proposed Method: We introduce SafeVLA, which wraps any VLA-based planner with a conformal prediction framework to produce trajectory prediction sets with statistically guaranteed coverage. First, we train a lightweight uncertainty estimator (via ensemble disagreement on tokenized trajectory logits) that quantifies distributional shift. At inference, conformal prediction calibrated on a held-out scene dataset produces a minimal trajectory set containing the ground-truth plan with user-specified probability (e.g., 90%). A safety monitor then checks all candidate trajectories against physical constraints and flags scenarios requiring human intervention or fallback to a conservative rule-based planner.

Experiments: (1) Coverage guarantee verification across nuPlan/Waymo test splits with increasing distributional shift (weather, time-of-day). (2) False-safety-alarm rate vs. coverage trade-off curves. (3) Closed-loop CARLA evaluation measuring collision rates when SafeVLA triggers fallback versus not. (4) Ablation on calibration set size and uncertainty estimator architecture. We demonstrate maintained AutoVLA performance in-distribution while providing formal safety bounds out-of-distribution.

title: SafetyGRPO: Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Safety-Critical Autonomous Driving Scenarios
description: Problem: AutoVLA's GRPO-based reinforcement fine-tuning optimizes planning performance but treats all scenarios uniformly in reward design, without explicitly encoding safety constraints (collision avoidance, traffic law compliance, pedestrian protection). In safety-critical edge cases—occlusions, sudden pedestrian crossings, emergency vehicles—the model may optimize trajectory smoothness at the expense of safety margins. Proposed Method: We introduce SafetyGRPO, extending AutoVLA's reinforcement fine-tuning with a constrained policy optimization framework. We decompose the reward into a primary planning reward and hard safety constraint signals derived from: (1) a learned safety critic trained on near-miss scenarios, (2) formal traffic rule encodings as differentiable constraints, and (3) uncertainty-weighted penalties when perception confidence is low. Crucially, we construct a 'safety-critical scenario bank' by mining rare dangerous events from nuPlan and Waymo, augmented with adversarial scenario generation, to ensure sufficient gradient signal for safety constraints during GRPO updates. The fast/slow thinking modes are extended with a third 'safety override' mode triggered by the critic. Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan safety-critical splits, a new adversarial CARLA benchmark with injected hazards, and collision/near-miss rates on Waymo. Ablations compare constraint enforcement strategies and analyze mode-switching frequency versus safety-performance tradeoffs.

title: SafeGuard-VLA: Uncertainty-Aware Conformal Prediction for Trajectory Verification in Vision-Language-Action Autonomous Driving Models
description:
Problem: While AutoVLA and similar VLA models achieve competitive planning performance, they lack principled uncertainty quantification mechanisms. In safety-critical autonomous driving, knowing *when* the model is uncertain is as important as the trajectory output itself—overconfident predictions in novel or adversarial scenarios can be catastrophic. Current VLA models provide no statistical guarantees on trajectory feasibility or safety margins.

Proposed Method: We introduce conformal prediction as a post-hoc calibration layer on top of frozen VLA trajectory outputs. During a calibration phase using held-out driving logs, we compute nonconformity scores measuring deviation between predicted and ground-truth trajectories. At inference time, we construct trajectory prediction sets with guaranteed coverage (e.g., 95% marginal coverage). Additionally, we train a lightweight uncertainty head that predicts conformal set size as an early-warning signal, triggering slow-thinking chain-of-thought reasoning only when uncertainty exceeds a threshold—replacing AutoVLA's heuristic fast/slow switching with statistically-grounded mode selection.

Experiments: (1) Coverage validity tests on nuScenes and Waymo held-out splits; (2) Ablation comparing conformal-triggered vs. heuristic reasoning switching on CARLA closed-loop benchmarks measuring collision rate and compute cost; (3) Out-of-distribution robustness evaluation under weather perturbations and adversarial agent behaviors; (4) Comparison against Monte Carlo Dropout and ensemble-based uncertainty baselines.

title: SafeGuard-VLA: Uncertainty-Aware Fallback Mechanisms for Vision-Language-Action Driving Models via Conformal Prediction
description:
Problem: End-to-end VLA models like AutoVLA can produce confident but dangerously wrong trajectory predictions in out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios—edge cases not well-represented during training. Current VLA architectures lack principled mechanisms to detect when the model is operating beyond its competence boundary and should defer to a safer fallback controller.

Proposed Method: We augment AutoVLA with a conformal prediction framework operating on the trajectory token distribution. At inference time, we construct prediction sets from calibration data (nuPlan/nuScenes held-out splits) that guarantee coverage at a user-specified confidence level (e.g., 95%). When the conformal prediction set exceeds a size threshold—indicating high uncertainty—the system triggers a hierarchical fallback: first activating slow-thinking chain-of-thought reasoning, then if uncertainty persists, deferring to a rule-based safety controller (e.g., constant deceleration or lane-keeping). The GRPO reward signal is extended to penalize unnecessary fallback activations in routine scenarios, encouraging the model to be calibrated rather than merely cautious.

Experiments: (1) OOD detection benchmarks on rare-scenario subsets of Waymo and nuPlan; (2) Closed-loop CARLA safety metrics (collision rate, fallback frequency) comparing conformal thresholds; (3) Calibration curves measuring coverage guarantees empirically; (4) Ablation over fallback hierarchy levels and conformal coverage rates.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Risk Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Models via Conformal Prediction
description:
Problem: While AutoVLA and similar VLA models demonstrate strong average-case performance, they lack principled uncertainty quantification—critical for safety-critical autonomous driving where rare edge cases demand reliable confidence estimates. Current VLA models either output overconfident trajectories or rely on heuristic safety checks disconnected from model uncertainty.

Proposed Method: We propose SafeVLA, which augments VLA-based planners with distribution-free uncertainty quantification using conformal prediction. During inference, SafeVLA generates an ensemble of candidate trajectories via stochastic decoding (temperature sampling over the discrete action tokens) and constructs a conformal prediction set with guaranteed coverage probability. When prediction set size exceeds a threshold (indicating high uncertainty), the model automatically triggers slow-thinking chain-of-thought reasoning and activates a conservative fallback policy. We additionally introduce a risk-stratified calibration procedure that separately calibrates uncertainty thresholds for distinct scenario categories (intersections, merges, pedestrian zones) using held-out calibration splits.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA closed-loop benchmarks, measuring: (1) calibration quality via Expected Calibration Error and coverage guarantee validity, (2) collision rate reduction versus AutoVLA baseline under distribution shift, (3) reasoning activation efficiency (unnecessary slow-thinking reduction), and (4) robustness under adversarial weather/sensor degradation. Ablations test calibration set size and scenario-stratification impact.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Abstention and Human Handoff in Vision-Language-Action Models for Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: Current VLA models like AutoVLA generate actions even in out-of-distribution or high-uncertainty scenarios (construction zones, adverse weather, novel pedestrian behaviors), which can be catastrophic. There is no principled mechanism for a VLA to recognize its own epistemic limits and safely defer to human control or a conservative fallback policy. Proposed Method: We augment AutoVLA's GRPO training with a learned abstention mechanism: the model outputs a calibrated uncertainty token alongside each trajectory, trained via a novel reward signal that penalizes both overconfident wrong predictions and excessive unnecessary abstentions. We use conformal prediction on the trajectory token distribution to produce coverage-guaranteed uncertainty bounds. When uncertainty exceeds a dynamic threshold (itself conditioned on scene context via a lightweight MLP head), the model triggers a structured handoff protocol—switching to a minimal-risk maneuver (pull over, reduce speed) while generating a natural-language explanation for the human operator. Training uses difficulty-stratified data augmentation, injecting corrupted/rare scenarios from nuPlan and CARLA. Experiments: (1) calibration curves comparing abstention accuracy vs. false-positive rates across weather/scenario types; (2) closed-loop safety metrics in CARLA with injected corner cases; (3) human study measuring operator trust and takeover quality when given model-generated explanations vs. no explanation. Baselines include threshold-based ensemble uncertainty and standard AutoVLA.

title: ReasonAware Distillation: Compressing VLA Reasoning Chains into Lightweight Driving Policies via Selective Chain-of-Thought Transfer
description: Problem: AutoVLA and similar slow-thinking VLA models produce high-quality trajectories via chain-of-thought reasoning, but inference latency from lengthy reasoning chains makes deployment on embedded automotive hardware impractical. Simply distilling final trajectories discards valuable intermediate reasoning that improves robustness in edge cases. Proposed Method: We introduce ReasonAware Distillation, a framework that selectively transfers reasoning chain knowledge from a large VLA teacher (e.g., AutoVLA-72B) to a compact student model (3B parameters). Using the teacher's adaptive reasoning mechanism as a signal, we identify 'reasoning-critical' scenarios (where slow thinking was triggered) and train the student with three objectives: (1) trajectory imitation loss on all samples, (2) compressed reasoning distillation loss that learns condensed 1-2 sentence rationales rather than full chains on critical scenarios, and (3) a reasoning-necessity classifier that mimics the teacher's fast/slow mode selection. The student learns when reasoning matters without always generating full chains. Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan, CARLA, and a new edge-case benchmark (construction zones, adversarial pedestrians) measuring L2 trajectory error, collision rate, and inference latency on NVIDIA Orin hardware. We compare against pure trajectory distillation, full chain distillation, and quantized AutoVLA baselines, targeting 10x speedup with <5% performance degradation.

title: SafetyGRPO: Constrained Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Safety-Critical Scenario Prioritization in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: While AutoVLA's GRPO-based reinforcement fine-tuning improves efficiency by reducing unnecessary reasoning in simple scenarios, it lacks explicit mechanisms to prioritize safety constraints in rare but critical edge cases (sudden pedestrian crossings, adverse weather, emergency vehicles). Standard reward signals optimizing trajectory accuracy may inadvertently under-weight catastrophic but low-frequency violations. Proposed Method: We introduce SafetyGRPO, a constrained variant of GRPO that augments the reward function with a hierarchical safety penalty structure. We decompose rewards into three tiers: (1) trajectory accuracy for nominal driving, (2) a hard constraint penalty for safety-critical rule violations (collision, red-light running), and (3) a soft penalty for discomfort metrics. Using Lagrangian relaxation, we dynamically balance these objectives during fine-tuning. Additionally, we construct a synthetic safety-augmented dataset by adversarially injecting edge-case scenarios into nuPlan/CARLA training distributions using diffusion-based scene perturbation, ensuring the model encounters sufficient safety-critical examples. Experiments: We evaluate on standard benchmarks (nuPlan, CARLA leaderboard) plus a curated safety-critical subset including adversarial pedestrians and occluded intersections. We measure collision rate, infraction frequency, and reasoning verbosity across scenario difficulty tiers. Ablations compare unconstrained GRPO, hard-constraint only, and full SafetyGRPO variants.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Confidence Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Models via Conformal Prediction
description:
Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates strong planning performance, VLA models for autonomous driving lack reliable uncertainty quantification — the model cannot distinguish when it should trust its fast-thinking trajectory versus escalate to human oversight or conservative fallback behaviors. Overconfident predictions in novel scenarios (unusual weather, adversarial road markings, edge-case pedestrian behavior) pose critical safety risks.

Method: We propose SafeVLA, augmenting AutoVLA's GRPO-trained backbone with conformal prediction sets over the discretized trajectory token space. During inference, we compute nonconformity scores over held-out calibration trajectories to produce statistically valid prediction sets with guaranteed coverage (e.g., 95%). When the prediction set contains multiple high-uncertainty trajectories, SafeVLA triggers slow-thinking mode or outputs a safety fallback (gradual deceleration). We additionally introduce a lightweight epistemic uncertainty head trained via Monte Carlo dropout over the vision encoder, enabling real-time uncertainty estimation without full ensemble overhead.

Experiments: (1) Calibration quality (ECE, reliability diagrams) on nuScenes and Waymo OOD splits; (2) Safety-critical scenario detection rate on CARLA adversarial benchmarks; (3) Fast/slow thinking mode switching accuracy versus ground-truth scenario complexity labels; (4) Ablation comparing conformal sets vs. softmax confidence vs. MC dropout; (5) Downstream collision rate when uncertainty triggers fallback behaviors.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Deferral in Vision-Language-Action Models for Safety-Critical Autonomous Driving Scenarios
description:
Problem: AutoVLA and similar VLA models produce trajectory outputs with uniform confidence, yet autonomous driving requires knowing *when* the model should defer to human oversight or fallback controllers—particularly in out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios like adverse weather, construction zones, or near-miss events where overconfident planning can be catastrophic.

Method: We propose SafeVLA, which augments a VLA backbone (initialized from AutoVLA) with a lightweight conformal prediction head that estimates trajectory-level uncertainty by aggregating token-level entropy across the autoregressive generation process. When uncertainty exceeds a calibrated threshold, SafeVLA triggers a 'deferral mode': it outputs an interpretable natural-language explanation of its uncertainty and transfers control to a modular safety controller. We further introduce an uncertainty-aware GRPO variant where the reward function penalizes high-confidence predictions on OOD inputs identified via a held-out calibration set, encouraging appropriate epistemic humility.

Experiments: (1) OOD robustness benchmarks on nuPlan and CARLA with synthetically injected distribution shifts (fog, night, novel road geometries); (2) Deferral precision-recall curves measuring whether high-uncertainty predictions correlate with actual collision-risk scenarios; (3) Human-in-the-loop simulation comparing safety outcomes of deferral vs. non-deferral baselines; (4) Ablation of conformal calibration set size and threshold selection strategies.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: Current VLA driving models like AutoVLA optimize for trajectory accuracy but lack explicit mechanisms to handle epistemic uncertainty and tail-risk scenarios (rare but catastrophic events like sudden pedestrian crossings or sensor occlusions). Standard GRPO-style fine-tuning rewards mean performance, potentially producing overconfident models that fail catastrophically in edge cases. Method: We propose SafeVLA, which augments the reinforcement fine-tuning stage with (1) a Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) objective that penalizes worst-case trajectory deviations rather than expected deviations, (2) an ensemble-based epistemic uncertainty estimator applied to tokenized trajectory logits that triggers slow-thinking chain-of-thought reasoning when uncertainty exceeds a learned threshold, and (3) a safety-critic reward signal derived from a separately trained occupancy prediction model that discounts rewards for trajectories passing near predicted occupied regions. Planned Experiments: We evaluate on CARLA closed-loop benchmarks with specifically constructed adversarial scenario suites (sudden cut-ins, occluded crossings), nuPlan reactive agents, and a new edge-case split of nuScenes. Metrics include collision rate, near-miss rate, CVaR of displacement error, and reasoning trigger calibration (ECE). Ablations isolate each component's contribution. We expect SafeVLA to substantially reduce tail-risk failures while maintaining competitive nominal performance.

title: AdverVLA: Adversarial Scenario Generation via Inverse Reinforcement Learning to Stress-Test Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: While AutoVLA and similar VLA models demonstrate strong average-case performance, their robustness in rare, safety-critical edge cases remains poorly characterized. Standard benchmarks lack sufficient adversarial diversity to expose failure modes in learned trajectory planners. Method: We propose AdverVLA, a framework that uses a trained VLA model (e.g., AutoVLA) as a surrogate to generate maximally adversarial driving scenarios. Specifically, we train an adversarial agent via Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) to infer reward functions that expose VLA policy weaknesses, then synthesize novel CARLA scenarios by perturbing agent behaviors, weather conditions, and road geometry using gradient signals from the VLA's trajectory outputs. A secondary safety critic network flags physically dangerous predicted trajectories. The adversarial scenarios are curated into a benchmark suite and used in a second GRPO fine-tuning loop to harden the VLA. Experiments: (1) Measure collision/infraction rates of AutoVLA, UniAD, and SparseDrive under AdverVLA-generated scenarios vs. standard benchmarks; (2) Evaluate whether adversarial fine-tuning improves closed-loop safety metrics on CARLA Leaderboard without degrading nuPlan open-loop accuracy; (3) Ablate IRL vs. random perturbation for adversarial scenario quality. This provides both a stress-testing methodology and a self-improving robustness loop for VLA driving models.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Trajectory Tokenization with Conservative Fallback for Safety-Critical Autonomous Driving Scenarios
description: Problem: AutoVLA and similar VLA models excel at average-case planning but lack explicit mechanisms to quantify uncertainty and gracefully degrade to conservative behaviors when encountering out-of-distribution or safety-critical scenarios (e.g., occlusions, near-miss collisions, construction zones). A single autoregressive model may confidently output physically feasible but contextually dangerous trajectories without signaling uncertainty. Proposed Method: We introduce SafeVLA, which augments the trajectory tokenization scheme with uncertainty tokens representing epistemic confidence intervals over predicted waypoints. During GRPO fine-tuning, we add a safety-aware reward signal combining trajectory feasibility, collision risk (estimated via Monte Carlo rollouts), and calibration quality (expected calibration error). A hierarchical fallback mechanism uses predicted uncertainty magnitude to dynamically switch between normal operation and a conservative rule-based fallback controller. The model learns when to defer to safety primitives rather than forcing autoregressive trajectory completion. Planned Experiments: (1) Evaluate calibration quality and collision rates on nuPlan and CARLA with injected adversarial agents; (2) Benchmark uncertainty estimation against MC-Dropout and ensemble baselines; (3) Measure fallback activation rates versus collision reduction in closed-loop CARLA scenarios with varying occlusion levels; (4) Ablate reward components to isolate safety-calibration tradeoffs, targeting 30% collision reduction with minimal comfort degradation.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Fallback Triggering in Vision-Language-Action Models via Epistemic Calibration
description: Problem: AutoVLA and similar VLA models adaptively switch between fast and slow reasoning modes, but lack principled mechanisms to detect when the model's confidence in its planned trajectory is too low to act safely—potentially leading to overconfident failures in out-of-distribution or safety-critical scenarios (e.g., sudden pedestrian occlusion, sensor degradation, rare weather). Proposed Method: We augment the VLA with an epistemic uncertainty head trained via conformal prediction over trajectory token distributions. During inference, if the trajectory uncertainty exceeds a learned threshold, the model triggers a 'safe fallback' mode: it generates an explicit uncertainty-annotated chain-of-thought, queries a conservative rule-based planner for a safe maneuver (e.g., controlled deceleration), and flags the scenario for human review. We use Monte Carlo dropout and ensemble disagreement across trajectory token logits as uncertainty signals, calibrated on held-out nuPlan validation splits. GRPO fine-tuning is extended with a safety-penalty reward that penalizes overconfident wrong trajectories more than abstentions. Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan, CARLA adversarial benchmarks, and a synthetic OOD corruption suite (rain, fog, sensor noise). Metrics include trajectory error, collision rate, false-positive abstention rate, and calibration ECE. Ablations compare uncertainty estimators and fallback strategies.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Risk Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Models via Conformal Prediction
description:
Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates adaptive reasoning and reinforcement fine-tuning for autonomous driving, it lacks principled uncertainty quantification — the model produces point-estimate trajectories without communicating when its predictions are unreliable, which is critical for safety-critical deployment.

Proposed Method: We integrate conformal prediction into the VLA framework to produce statistically guaranteed prediction sets for trajectory planning. During inference, we construct trajectory confidence regions using split conformal prediction on tokenized action sequences, providing coverage guarantees without distributional assumptions. We introduce a risk-stratified action head that outputs multiple candidate trajectories with calibrated confidence intervals, where coverage tightness serves as a real-time risk signal. When uncertainty exceeds learned thresholds, the model automatically escalates to slow-thinking (chain-of-thought) reasoning mode, creating a safety-aware version of adaptive reasoning. We additionally propose a GRPO-compatible reward that penalizes overconfident failures while rewarding tight-but-correct prediction sets.

Experiments: (1) Coverage calibration on nuPlan/nuScenes held-out splits across scenario difficulty tiers; (2) Ablation of fast vs. slow thinking activation thresholds against uncertainty scores; (3) Closed-loop CARLA evaluation measuring collision rate reduction when uncertainty-triggered slow thinking is active; (4) Comparison against Monte Carlo Dropout and ensemble baselines on calibration metrics (ECE, coverage gap) and planning accuracy.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Causal Reasoning for Safety-Critical Scenario Understanding in Vision-Language-Action Models
description: Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates adaptive reasoning for typical driving scenarios, VLA models remain brittle in rare safety-critical edge cases (e.g., sudden pedestrian crossings, cut-ins, adverse weather) because chain-of-thought reasoning is correlational rather than causal — models learn surface patterns without understanding interventional consequences of actions. Method: We propose CausalVLA, which augments VLA training with counterfactual causal reasoning. During slow-thinking mode, the model is trained to generate explicit counterfactual traces: 'If I had taken action A instead of B, the outcome would have been X because Y.' We construct a counterfactual training dataset by mining near-miss events from nuPlan and Waymo, using a physics simulator (CARLA) to render alternative trajectory outcomes. We extend GRPO with a causal consistency reward that penalizes contradictions between predicted counterfactuals and simulated ground-truth outcomes. A lightweight causal graph module extracts object-level dependencies from scene tokens to condition trajectory generation. Experiments: (1) Safety-critical scenario benchmarks (CARLA NoCrash, Waymo interaction scenarios), (2) out-of-distribution generalization on unseen edge cases, (3) counterfactual reasoning faithfulness evaluated via simulation rollouts, (4) ablation of causal reward vs. standard trajectory reward, comparing collision rates and reasoning coherence against AutoVLA baseline.

title: SafetyGRPO: Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Safety-Critical Scenario Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models
description: Problem: While AutoVLA's GRPO-based reinforcement fine-tuning improves planning efficiency in routine scenarios, it lacks explicit mechanisms to prioritize safety constraints in rare but critical situations (pedestrian crossings, emergency vehicles, adverse weather). Standard reward formulations optimize trajectory accuracy without distinguishing between benign planning errors and safety violations, potentially learning efficient but dangerous behaviors. Proposed Method: We introduce SafetyGRPO, a constrained reinforcement fine-tuning framework that augments GRPO with a dual-reward structure: a primary trajectory reward and a hard safety constraint penalty derived from a learned safety critic trained on near-miss scenarios. The safety critic is pretrained on augmented adversarial scenarios generated via diffusion-based scene perturbation (injecting occlusions, sudden obstacles, edge-case agents). During GRPO rollouts, trajectories violating safety constraints receive multiplicative reward penalties regardless of planning accuracy, forcing the policy to develop safety-aware slow thinking specifically for high-risk contexts. We further introduce a safety-triggered reasoning gate that activates chain-of-thought only when the safety critic detects elevated risk, making reasoning both adaptive and safety-responsive. Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan safety-critical splits, CARLA adversarial scenarios, and a newly constructed SafetyBench dataset of 500 near-crash scenarios extracted from Waymo Open Dataset. Metrics include collision rate, time-to-collision, infraction frequency, and reasoning activation rate across risk levels.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Risk Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Models via Conformal Prediction
description:
Problem: While AutoVLA and similar VLA models demonstrate strong average-case planning performance, they lack principled uncertainty quantification — a critical safety gap for deployment. When a VLA model is confidently wrong (e.g., misreading an occluded pedestrian), there is no mechanism to trigger fallback behaviors or request human intervention. Current approaches treat action outputs as point estimates without coverage guarantees.

Proposed Method: We augment a VLA model (built on AutoVLA's architecture) with conformal prediction to produce statistically valid prediction sets over discretized trajectory tokens. Using a held-out calibration split, we compute nonconformity scores between predicted and ground-truth trajectory tokens, constructing adaptive trajectory sets that guarantee user-specified coverage (e.g., 95%). We propose a risk-stratified routing mechanism: when the conformal set is small (low uncertainty), the model executes autonomously; when large (high uncertainty), it triggers slow-thinking chain-of-thought reasoning or escalates to a safety fallback controller. Experiments: Evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA with metrics including marginal/conditional coverage rates, set size efficiency, false safety rate (confident wrong predictions), and downstream planning performance. title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Reasoning for Safety-Critical Scenario Generalization in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:
Problem: VLA models like AutoVLA trained on real-world driving data suffer from distribution shift in rare safety-critical scenarios (e.g., sudden pedestrian crossings, cut-ins, brake failures). Third, we design a counterfactual consistency reward for GRPO: the model's action outputs must change appropriately and proportionally when counterfactual observations are substituted, penalizing causal insensitivity. Experiments: (1) Closed-loop CARLA evaluation on rare/adversarial scenarios vs. AutoVLA baseline; (2) nuScenes safety-critical subset performance; (3) Ablation on counterfactual reward weight and scenario diversity; (4) Human evaluation of causal reasoning quality in chain-of-thought outputs; (5) Out-of-distribution generalization benchmarks from CARLA leaderboard challenge scenarios.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Intervention Training for Causally-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving

We further introduce a causal attribution head that identifies which visual elements most influenced the action, supervised via intervention labels. Training combines standard GRPO-style RL fine-tuning with the causal consistency regularizer. Experiments: We evaluate on CARLA closed-loop benchmarks under systematic distribution shift (new weather, new towns), spurious correlation stress tests, and intervention-based causal fidelity metrics. We compare against AutoVLA and ablations removing causal components, measuring collision rate, route completion, and causal attribution accuracy.

title: SafetyGRPO: Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Safety-Critical Scenario Planning in Vision-Language-Action Models
description:

Experiments: (1) Standard benchmarks: nuPlan, nuScenes, Waymo open-loop metrics; (2) Safety-critical closed-loop CARLA scenarios (cut-ins, sudden braking, pedestrian occlusion); (3) Ablation on reward decomposition components; (4) Reasoning frequency analysis comparing AutoVLA-GRPO vs SafetyGRPO on scenario risk level; (5) Transfer evaluation on real-world edge-case dashcam dataset.

title: SafeReason: Uncertainty-Aware Chain-of-Thought Grounding for Safety-Critical Scenario Detection in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates adaptive reasoning for trajectory planning, VLA models lack explicit mechanisms to detect and verbalize uncertainty in safety-critical edge cases (e.g., sudden pedestrian occlusion, adversarial agents, sensor degradation). title: GRPO-Calibrated Uncertainty: Teaching VLA Models to Know When They Don't Know in Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: Current VLA models for autonomous driving, including AutoVLA, produce deterministic trajectory outputs without expressing epistemic uncertainty. Proposed Method: We extend the GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning paradigm with an uncertainty-aware reward signal. The model outputs both a trajectory and a calibrated confidence score as part of its autoregressive generation. We define rewards that jointly optimize: (1) trajectory accuracy when confidence is high, (2) appropriate abstention/handoff when confidence is low and the scenario is genuinely difficult (measured by ensemble disagreement as a proxy for ground-truth difficulty), and (3) penalize overconfident failures. We introduce a lightweight ensemble disagreement estimator using Monte Carlo token dropout during inference to generate pseudo-ground-truth difficulty labels for reward computation. Planned Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA with held-out distribution-shift scenarios (fog, rain, construction zones). Metrics include Expected Calibration Error (ECE) for confidence scores, collision rate when deferring vs. acting, and trajectory quality at varying confidence thresholds. Ablations compare reward formulations and dropout rates.

title: SafetyGRPO: Constrained Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Safety-Critical Scenario Planning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:
Problem: AutoVLA and similar VLA models use GRPO to optimize trajectory planning quality, but GRPO's reward signal focuses on trajectory accuracy metrics (displacement error, comfort). Proposed Method: We introduce SafetyGRPO, extending GRPO with a constrained multi-objective reward framework specifically designed for safety-critical driving. We decompose the reward into (1) a standard trajectory quality term, (2) a hard constraint penalty for safety violations (collisions, TTC violations, lane infractions) modeled as a Lagrangian multiplier updated online, and (3) a 'safety reasoning bonus' that rewards chain-of-thought outputs containing explicit hazard identification before trajectory generation. We further construct a curated safety-critical fine-tuning dataset by mining rare adversarial scenarios from nuPlan, CARLA adversarial benchmarks, and synthetic perturbations via surrogate vehicle behavior injection.

Experiments: (1) Safety metric evaluation on CARLA's Town05-Long and Bench2Drive benchmarks measuring collision rate and infraction scores; (2) Ablation of reward components; (3) Analysis of reasoning verbosity in safety-critical vs. normal scenarios; (4) Cross-dataset transfer to nuPlan reactive agents. title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Intervention Training for Causal Scene Understanding in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:

The model is trained with a contrastive causal objective that enforces: (1) trajectory outputs should change appropriately when causally relevant factors are intervened upon, and (2) trajectory outputs should remain stable under spurious factor interventions. We integrate this into the GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning stage by adding counterfactual consistency as an auxiliary reward signal alongside trajectory accuracy rewards.

Experiments: Evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA with held-out distribution shifts (weather, density, adversarial agents). Measure: causal consistency scores via automated counterfactual probing, closed-loop safety metrics under OOD conditions, and a new 'what-if query answering' benchmark where models predict trajectory changes under hypothetical interventions. title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Risk Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Models via Conformal Prediction
description:
Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates adaptive reasoning and RL fine-tuning for autonomous driving, it lacks principled uncertainty quantification — the model cannot reliably signal when its trajectory predictions are uncertain or potentially unsafe, which is critical for real-world deployment and handoff to human drivers. Current VLA models produce point estimates without calibrated confidence measures.

Proposed Method: We introduce SafeVLA, which augments a VLA backbone (similar to AutoVLA) with conformal prediction to produce statistically guaranteed trajectory uncertainty sets. During inference, instead of outputting a single tokenized trajectory, SafeVLA generates a prediction region containing the true trajectory with user-specified coverage probability (e.g., 95%). We propose scenario-conditional conformal sets that adapt coverage based on scene complexity detected by the reasoning chain — tight sets for simple straight-road scenarios and wider sets for complex intersections. A risk-aware action selection module then chooses the trajectory minimizing expected collision cost within the conformal set. We further train a lightweight uncertainty token that summarizes prediction confidence, enabling efficient fast-thinking mode while preserving safety guarantees.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA closed-loop benchmarks measuring (1) empirical coverage validity, (2) collision rate reduction vs. AutoVLA baseline, (3) prediction set size efficiency across scenario complexities, and (4) intervention trigger accuracy for human-handoff scenarios.

title: SafeGuard-VLA: Uncertainty-Aware Conformal Prediction for Runtime Safety Monitoring of Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:

description:

title: SafeGuard-VLA: Uncertainty-Aware Abstention and Human Handoff in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: AutoVLA and similar VLA driving models adaptively switch between fast and slow reasoning, but neither mode addresses when the model should abstain from acting entirely and request human intervention. We further introduce a third thinking mode—'cautious thinking'—that combines chain-of-thought with explicit uncertainty verbalization before trajectory generation. Experiments: (1) abstention precision-recall on held-out OOD scenarios vs. baselines; (2) downstream collision rate when abstention triggers fallback vs. forced execution; (3) calibration curves (ECE) across standard and adversarial splits; (4) human study on operator trust when receiving abstention rationales. title: SafeGuard-VLA: Uncertainty-Aware Fallback Mechanisms for Vision-Language-Action Models via Conformal Prediction
description: Problem: VLA models like AutoVLA generate trajectories directly from language models, but lack principled uncertainty quantification — they cannot reliably detect when their predictions are untrustworthy, risking safety-critical failures in novel or adversarial scenarios. We additionally train a lightweight uncertainty-conditioned router using GRPO that learns when to defer to the fallback versus proceeding with VLA output. Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA closed-loop benchmarks, measuring (1) collision rate under distribution-shifted weather/traffic conditions, (2) calibration quality (coverage vs. set size tradeoffs), (3) intervention rate and latency overhead compared to AutoVLA baseline, and (4) ablations on fallback policy aggressiveness thresholds.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Reasoning for Safety-Critical Scenario Generalization in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: VLA models like AutoVLA excel at common driving scenarios but struggle with rare safety-critical edge cases (e.g., sudden pedestrian crossings, cut-ins, adverse weather) due to data imbalance. title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Scenario Augmentation for Robust Causal Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:
Problem: VLA models like AutoVLA learn correlational patterns from driving demonstrations but may fail in out-of-distribution causal scenarios (e.g., sudden pedestrian emergence, adversarial cut-ins). The chain-of-thought reasoning they produce may reflect spurious correlations rather than genuine causal understanding of scene dynamics, leading to unsafe generalization.

We train the VLA with a dual objective: (1) standard trajectory imitation, and (2) a counterfactual consistency loss that penalizes the model when its reasoning and actions fail to change appropriately under semantically meaningful scene perturbations. During GRPO fine-tuning, rewards additionally measure causal fidelity — whether the model's verbal reasoning correctly identifies the causally relevant objects that changed.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA closed-loop benchmarks with injected adversarial events, measuring collision rate, reasoning correctness (via LLM-as-judge on counterfactual pairs), and out-of-distribution generalization. title: SafetyGRPO: Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Collision-Critical Scenarios in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: AutoVLA and similar VLA models use GRPO to optimize trajectory quality and reasoning efficiency, but GRPO's reward formulation treats all scenarios uniformly, potentially under-penalizing safety-critical failures (e.g., near-miss collisions, red-light violations) relative to comfort or efficiency metrics. We define a hierarchical reward structure: a primary safety reward (collision-free trajectory, traffic rule compliance) that acts as a constraint floor, and secondary rewards (efficiency, comfort, reasoning brevity) optimized only when safety is satisfied. We additionally construct a Safety-Critical Scenario Buffer by mining edge cases from nuPlan and CARLA simulations—sudden pedestrian crossings, cut-in vehicles, brake failures—and oversample these during fine-tuning with increased constraint weights. Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan, CARLA Safety Benchmarks, and CommonRoad against AutoVLA and baseline GRPO fine-tuning. Metrics include collision rate, traffic violation rate, comfort scores, and scenario-specific success rates. We ablate constraint weights, buffer sampling ratios, and Lagrangian update schedules to characterize safety-efficiency tradeoffs.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Reasoning Gating for Safety-Critical Scenario Detection in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:
Problem: AutoVLA's adaptive reasoning selection (fast vs. slow thinking) relies on GRPO-learned policies that may fail to trigger deliberate reasoning precisely when safety is most critical — edge cases like occluded pedestrians, adversarial road users, or rare weather conditions. A missed slow-thinking activation in these scenarios could be catastrophic, yet current approaches have no explicit safety-aware gating mechanism.

Proposed Method: We introduce SafeVLA, which augments the reasoning-mode selector with a lightweight uncertainty quantification head trained via conformal prediction on scenario embeddings. The head estimates epistemic uncertainty over the visual scene and compares it against calibrated safety-critical thresholds derived from a curated near-miss dataset. When uncertainty exceeds thresholds, SafeVLA forces slow-thinking chain-of-thought reasoning regardless of the base policy's preference. Additionally, we introduce a contrastive safety-scenario dataset (SafeDrive-100K) synthesized via diffusion-based augmentation of rare hazardous events to improve calibration.

Experiments: (1) Ablation on nuPlan and CARLA comparing reasoning trigger accuracy under rare vs. common scenarios. (2) Closed-loop safety metrics (collision rate, TTC violations) vs. AutoVLA baseline. (3) Calibration error analysis of uncertainty estimates. (4) Latency-safety trade-off curves showing minimal overhead in routine driving while dramatically increasing slow-thinking activation in safety-critical conditions.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Scenario Augmentation for Causal Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: Current VLA driving models like AutoVLA learn correlations between visual scenes and actions but lack explicit causal understanding—they cannot reliably distinguish whether a planned action is causally safe or merely correlated with safe outcomes in training data. Additionally, we introduce a causal chain-of-thought supervision signal that explicitly labels which scene elements causally influenced the planning decision, integrated into the GRPO reward shaping. Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan closed-loop benchmarks with adversarial perturbations, CARLA challenge scenarios, and a new counterfactual robustness benchmark derived from Waymo. We measure causal faithfulness of reasoning chains via human evaluation and intervention consistency scores, demonstrating improved safety and generalization over AutoVLA baselines.

title: SafeReason-VLA: Uncertainty-Aware Safety Constraints for Vision-Language-Action Models via Constrained Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
description: Problem: AutoVLA and similar VLA models optimize for trajectory accuracy but lack explicit safety guarantees—the model may produce plausible-looking but unsafe trajectories in rare edge cases (pedestrian occlusion, adversarial weather), and GRPO-style fine-tuning optimizes reward without formal safety constraints. A safety critic head is trained jointly to predict constraint violations, enabling dual reward shaping: performance reward plus safety penalty. Experiments: (1) Closed-loop CARLA evaluation under adversarial perturbations and rare scenario injection; (2) nuPlan safety metrics (collision rate, comfort violations) comparing vanilla GRPO vs. C-GRPO; (3) Ablation on uncertainty threshold for triggering slow thinking; (4) Human evaluation of generated safety reasoning chains for interpretability. title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Reasoning Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Models via Conformal Prediction

title: SafeThink: Uncertainty-Aware Chain-of-Thought Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Models via Conformal Prediction
description: Problem: While AutoVLA's adaptive reasoning (fast vs. slow thinking) improves efficiency, neither mode provides calibrated uncertainty estimates for its trajectory outputs. title: SafetyGRPO: Constrained Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for VLA Models with Hard Safety Guarantees in Autonomous Driving
description: Problem: While AutoVLA's GRPO-based reinforcement fine-tuning improves planning efficiency, it optimizes purely for trajectory quality metrics without explicit safety constraints. Additionally, we train a lightweight safety critic that flags high-risk trajectory proposals before execution, enabling the model to trigger slow-thinking chain-of-thought reasoning specifically for unsafe situations rather than simple ones. Planned Experiments: We evaluate on CARLA closed-loop benchmarks (infraction rates, route completion), nuPlan reactive simulation (safety-critical scenarios), and an adversarial pedestrian dataset. title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Reasoning for Safety-Critical Scenario Understanding in Vision-Language-Action Models
description:
Problem: Current VLA models like AutoVLA excel at trajectory planning but lack explicit causal understanding of why certain actions are unsafe — they cannot reason counterfactually ('what would have happened if I had turned left instead?'). Experiments: We evaluate on (1) CARLA closed-loop with adversarial agents targeting edge cases, (2) a curated safety-critical subset of nuPlan with near-miss scenarios, (3) a new counterfactual reasoning benchmark where models must rank trajectory alternatives by predicted safety. title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Scenario Augmentation for Causal Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: Current VLA driving models like AutoVLA learn correlations between scenes and actions but lack explicit causal understanding — they cannot distinguish whether a braking decision was caused by a pedestrian, traffic light, or spurious background features. title: SafeGuard-VLA: Uncertainty-Aware Rejection Sampling and Conformal Prediction for Safety-Critical Trajectory Validation in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:

Experiments: (1) Coverage validity and efficiency (set size) across nuPlan/Waymo scenarios stratified by severity; (2) Closed-loop CARLA safety metrics (collision rate, TTC violations) comparing fixed vs. uncertainty-triggered reasoning modes; (3) Ablations on calibration set size, coverage level, and conformal score design; (4) Computational overhead analysis.

title: SafetyShield-VLA: Uncertainty-Aware Safety Constraint Learning for Vision-Language-Action Driving Models via Constrained Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
description:

Experiments: We evaluate on CARLA closed-loop benchmarks with adversarial scenario injection (sudden pedestrian crossings, cut-ins), nuPlan reactive simulation with rule-violation detection, and a curated safety-critical subset of Waymo Open Dataset. title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Causal Reasoning for Interpretable Failure Mode Discovery in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
