title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Risk Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Models via Conformal Prediction and Adaptive Intervention
description:
Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates strong planning performance, VLA models for autonomous driving lack principled uncertainty quantification—they cannot reliably communicate when their trajectory predictions are overconfident or when human/safety intervention should be triggered. This gap is critical for deployment in safety-critical scenarios where distribution shift or adversarial conditions may cause silent failures.

Proposed Method: We augment a VLA backbone (built on AutoVLA's architecture) with conformal prediction to produce statistically valid trajectory prediction sets with guaranteed coverage under mild exchangeability assumptions. During inference, the model outputs a set of feasible trajectory candidates rather than a single action. We train a lightweight risk head that maps uncertainty set size and semantic reasoning tokens to a continuous risk score. When risk exceeds a learned threshold, the system adaptively switches from fast-thinking to slow-thinking mode (mirroring AutoVLA's dual modes) or requests human takeover. We apply GRPO fine-tuning with an additional coverage reward term to encourage well-calibrated, compact prediction sets.

Experiments: (1) Calibration evaluation on nuPlan and nuScenes measuring prediction set coverage vs. size trade-offs. (2) Intervention trigger accuracy in safety-critical CARLA scenarios (obstacles, adverse weather). (3) Ablation of fast/slow mode switching thresholds. (4) Human study measuring operator trust when uncertainty estimates are communicated visually.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Risk Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Models via Conformal Prediction and Safety-Constrained GRPO
description: Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates adaptive reasoning and trajectory planning, current VLA models for autonomous driving lack principled uncertainty quantification and safety guarantees. When the model is uncertain about a trajectory decision, it should either trigger slow-thinking mode or hand control back to a fallback system—but no rigorous mechanism exists to calibrate when VLA outputs are trustworthy enough to execute. Proposed Method: We introduce SafeVLA, which augments VLA-based driving with conformal prediction to produce distribution-free, statistically valid uncertainty sets over tokenized trajectory outputs. A lightweight conformal calibration head is trained post-hoc on a held-out calibration set, producing coverage-guaranteed prediction sets for each trajectory token. These uncertainty estimates gate fast/slow thinking mode selection: high-uncertainty predictions trigger chain-of-thought reasoning or fallback. Additionally, we extend GRPO with safety-constraint penalties derived from conformal coverage violations, penalizing reward updates that would degrade calibration quality. Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA closed-loop benchmarks, measuring (1) collision rate reduction, (2) calibration quality (empirical coverage vs. guaranteed coverage), (3) reasoning mode activation rates in uncertain vs. clear scenarios, and (4) planning accuracy under distribution shift using out-of-distribution weather/lighting conditions from CARLA. Baselines include AutoVLA and vanilla uncertainty-unaware VLAs.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Scenario Augmentation for Robust Causal Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: VLA models like AutoVLA learn correlations between visual contexts and actions but may exploit spurious statistical shortcuts rather than understanding causal structure (e.g., braking because pedestrians are typically near crosswalks, not because of actual collision risk). This leads to brittle generalization under distribution shift. Method: We propose CausalVLA, which augments training with automatically generated counterfactual scenarios using a scene graph editor and diffusion-based image synthesis. For each training scenario, we generate counterfactual variants by intervening on causal factors (e.g., removing a pedestrian, changing traffic light state, altering road geometry) while keeping confounders constant. We introduce a contrastive causal consistency loss that enforces the model's reasoning and action outputs to change appropriately under causal interventions but remain stable under non-causal perturbations (lighting, texture). We additionally fine-tune using GRPO with a causal reward that penalizes actions inconsistent with counterfactual ground truth trajectories. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes and CARLA with constructed causal intervention benchmarks measuring sensitivity to causal vs. spurious features, out-of-distribution generalization to rare edge cases, and closed-loop safety metrics. Ablations isolate contributions of counterfactual augmentation versus the contrastive loss versus GRPO causal reward.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Scenario Augmentation for Causal Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: Current VLA driving models like AutoVLA learn correlational patterns between observations and actions, lacking genuine causal understanding of how interventions (e.g., a pedestrian stepping out, a traffic light changing) causally necessitate specific trajectory decisions. This limits robustness to rare but critical edge cases and makes model reasoning difficult to verify causally. Proposed Method: We introduce CausalVLA, which augments VLA training with counterfactual scenario pairs generated via a neural scene editor. For each driving scenario, we automatically synthesize counterfactual variants by intervening on specific scene elements (remove pedestrian, change traffic light state, alter vehicle trajectory) using a diffusion-based scene editor conditioned on 3D scene graphs. We then train the VLA with a causal consistency loss: the model's chain-of-thought reasoning must correctly identify which scene elements causally influenced the trajectory change between original and counterfactual pairs, supervised via contrastive reasoning alignment. We additionally introduce a GRPO reward that scores causal attribution accuracy alongside trajectory quality. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes and CARLA with counterfactual evaluation benchmarks measuring trajectory sensitivity to causal interventions, out-of-distribution generalization, and reasoning faithfulness scores. We compare against AutoVLA baseline and ablate counterfactual augmentation quantity, causal loss weight, and scene editor fidelity.

title: SafeGuard-VLA: Uncertainty-Aware Hallucination Detection and Safe Action Abstention in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:
Problem: AutoVLA and similar VLA models can generate confidently wrong trajectory predictions when encountering out-of-distribution scenarios (unusual weather, rare road configurations, adversarial conditions). Unlike language tasks where hallucinations cause text errors, in autonomous driving they cause collisions. Current VLA models lack mechanisms to detect when their own reasoning is unreliable and defer to safer fallback behaviors.

Proposed Method: We augment AutoVLA's GRPO training with an uncertainty-aware abstention head that learns to predict epistemic uncertainty over trajectory tokens. We introduce a three-tier action policy: (1) confident execution, (2) conservative execution with reduced speed/increased margins, and (3) safe abstention requesting human takeover. We train this via a novel reward formulation that penalizes confident predictions on scenarios where the model's trajectory deviates significantly from ground truth, rewarding calibrated abstention. We additionally use conformal prediction on trajectory token distributions to provide statistically guaranteed coverage bounds, converting raw uncertainty scores into actionable safety thresholds.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA with injected OOD perturbations (fog, rare intersection types, sensor dropout). Metrics include abstention precision-recall curves, collision rate under abstention policies, calibration error (ECE), and closed-loop safety benchmarks. We compare against temperature scaling, MC-dropout, and ensemble baselines, demonstrating that targeted abstention reduces collision rates by >30% with minimal unnecessary intervention overhead.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Intervention Training for Interpretable Causal Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:
Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates adaptive chain-of-thought reasoning for trajectory planning, it remains unclear whether the model's reasoning reflects genuine causal understanding of driving scenarios or exploits spurious correlations between visual features and actions. A model may produce plausible-sounding reasoning chains while actually making planning decisions based on confounded shortcuts, leading to unsafe generalization in novel environments.

Proposed Method: We introduce CausalVLA, which augments VLA training with structured counterfactual intervention. During training, we construct counterfactual scene pairs by synthetically modifying critical causal factors (e.g., removing pedestrians, altering traffic light states, changing weather conditions) using NeRF-based and diffusion-based scene editing. We train the model to predict both original and counterfactual trajectories while explicitly generating counterfactual reasoning chains explaining how the intervention changed the decision. We introduce a causal consistency loss that penalizes contradictions between stated reasoning and trajectory differences across counterfactual pairs. We further use GRPO-style reinforcement fine-tuning with a reward that scores both trajectory accuracy and causal reasoning fidelity.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan, CARLA, and a new counterfactual driving benchmark we construct from Waymo Open Dataset. Metrics include standard planning performance, causal intervention accuracy (does trajectory change appropriately?), and out-of-distribution generalization. We compare against AutoVLA, DriveLM, and standard CoT-finetuned baselines.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Risk Calibration for Vision-Language-Action Driving Models via Conformal Prediction
description: Problem: AutoVLA and similar VLA models produce point-estimate trajectory outputs without reliable uncertainty quantification, making it difficult to know when to trust the model's plan versus defer to a safety fallback. In safety-critical driving, overconfident predictions in novel or adversarial scenarios can be catastrophic. Proposed Method: We augment a VLA model (built on AutoVLA's architecture) with conformal prediction to produce statistically valid prediction sets over tokenized trajectory actions. During inference, instead of emitting a single trajectory token sequence, the model outputs a calibrated prediction region guaranteeing that the true safe trajectory is included with user-specified coverage probability (e.g., 95%). We introduce a scenario-difficulty score derived from the chain-of-thought reasoning length and token entropy to dynamically tighten or relax coverage thresholds—tight coverage in simple scenes, wider sets in ambiguous ones. When prediction set size exceeds a threshold, a rule-based fallback planner takes control. We further fine-tune using a coverage-constrained GRPO variant that rewards small prediction sets while maintaining coverage guarantees. Experiments: Evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA closed-loop benchmarks measuring (1) empirical coverage validity, (2) average prediction set size, (3) collision rate with/without fallback, and (4) false-alarm rate compared to fixed-threshold baselines. Ablations isolate the contribution of reasoning-length-guided calibration.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Hallucination Detection and Safe Fallback for Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: VLA models like AutoVLA can produce confidently wrong trajectories in out-of-distribution scenarios (e.g., unusual weather, edge-case road geometries), where the model's language-generation confidence fails to correlate with physical safety. There is no principled mechanism to detect when the VLA is 'hallucinating' a plausible-sounding but dangerous plan. Proposed Method: We introduce an uncertainty-aware safety wrapper for autoregressive VLA driving models. First, we train an auxiliary conformal prediction head that calibrates token-level uncertainty scores during trajectory generation, using held-out nuPlan/Waymo driving logs. When uncertainty exceeds a learned threshold, the model triggers a lightweight rule-based fallback controller (MPC with conservative constraints) rather than executing the VLA-generated trajectory. Second, we finetune the VLA using a novel 'safety-aware GRPO' reward that penalizes high-uncertainty trajectory outputs in hindsight, encouraging the model to either produce confident safe plans or explicitly defer via a special <DEFER> token. Experiments: (1) OOD robustness benchmarks on nuPlan with corrupted sensor inputs; (2) CARLA closed-loop evaluation under adversarial weather; (3) ablation of conformal calibration thresholds vs. collision rates; (4) comparison of intervention frequency vs. safety improvement trade-off against AutoVLA and standard uncertainty baselines. We expect >30% reduction in safety-critical failures with <5% increase in fallback rate.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Intervention Training for Causal Scene Understanding in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates strong end-to-end driving performance, VLA models trained via imitation and GRPO-style RL may learn spurious correlations between scene context and actions (e.g., associating good weather with aggressive maneuvers) rather than causal relationships. This leads to brittle generalization under distribution shift — critical for safety. Proposed Method: We introduce CausalVLA, which augments VLA training with counterfactual intervention examples generated via a causal scene graph. For each training scenario, we automatically construct counterfactual variants by intervening on identified causal factors (e.g., occluding a pedestrian, changing traffic light state, altering weather) using diffusion-based image editing and physics-aware trajectory relabeling. We then apply a contrastive causal consistency loss: the model's trajectory outputs must change appropriately under causal interventions but remain stable under non-causal ones (e.g., background texture changes). This is integrated into the GRPO fine-tuning phase as an additional reward signal measuring causal sensitivity. Experiments: We evaluate on nuScenes and CARLA with held-out causal intervention test suites (e.g., suddenly appearing pedestrians, signal changes) measuring collision rate, reaction distance, and trajectory deviation under spurious vs. causal perturbations. We compare against AutoVLA, standard data augmentation baselines, and measure reasoning chain quality via human evaluation of causal explanation accuracy.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Reasoning Augmentation for Robust Causal Scene Understanding in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates adaptive reasoning for trajectory planning, VLA models for autonomous driving remain brittle to distribution shifts because they learn correlations rather than causal relationships between scene elements and actions. A model that performs well in normal driving may fail when spurious correlations (e.g., road color, lighting conditions) dominate over genuine causal factors (e.g., pedestrian intent, vehicle trajectories). Method: We propose CausalVLA, which augments VLA training with counterfactual scene reasoning. During training, we automatically generate counterfactual visual-language pairs by (1) using diffusion-based image editing to modify causally-relevant scene elements (remove/add pedestrians, change traffic light states) and (2) prompting the language model to generate counterfactual 'what-if' reasoning chains that explain how the trajectory should change. We introduce a contrastive causal consistency loss that enforces: factual and counterfactual trajectories diverge appropriately when causal elements change, but remain stable under non-causal perturbations (weather, texture). We additionally fine-tune with GRPO using a causal fidelity reward that measures trajectory sensitivity to causal vs. non-causal edits. Experiments: Evaluate on nuScenes and CARLA with held-out distribution shifts, OOD robustness benchmarks (nuScenes-C), and a new counterfactual consistency metric measuring trajectory invariance to non-causal perturbations, demonstrating improved causal understanding and generalization over AutoVLA.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Failure Prediction and Recovery in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models via Conformal Prediction
description:
Problem: VLA models like AutoVLA generate trajectories autoregressively but provide no calibrated uncertainty estimates, making it impossible to know when the model is likely to fail before executing potentially dangerous actions. Current approaches lack principled mechanisms to detect distributional shift, edge cases, or low-confidence planning decisions at inference time.

Proposed Method: We augment AutoVLA with a conformal prediction framework operating over the discrete trajectory token space. During a calibration phase on held-out driving scenarios, we construct prediction sets for trajectory tokens with guaranteed coverage guarantees. We introduce a 'safety score' derived from nonconformity measures on the VLA's token probability distributions. When the safety score exceeds a learned threshold, the system (1) automatically triggers slow-thinking chain-of-thought reasoning, (2) requests human intervention, or (3) falls back to a conservative rule-based planner. We additionally train a lightweight recovery policy via GRPO that specializes in low-confidence scenarios identified during calibration.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA across distribution-shift scenarios (adverse weather, rare road configurations, sensor degradation). Metrics include coverage validity of conformal sets, false-negative rate for dangerous failures, collision reduction under uncertainty-triggered fallback, and latency overhead. Baselines include Monte Carlo dropout, ensemble uncertainty, and vanilla AutoVLA.

title: SafetyGuard-VLA: Uncertainty-Aware Safety Intervention for Vision-Language-Action Driving Models via Conformal Prediction
description: Problem: AutoVLA and similar VLA models adaptively switch between fast and slow thinking, but lack principled mechanisms to detect when the model is operating near its competence boundary — situations where even slow thinking may produce unsafe trajectories. Current approaches rely on reward signals during GRPO training but cannot provide formal safety guarantees at deployment time. Proposed Method: We augment VLA models with a conformal prediction wrapper that produces statistically valid uncertainty sets over tokenized trajectory actions. During inference, if the conformal prediction set exceeds a calibrated coverage threshold (indicating distributional shift or genuine ambiguity), the system triggers a safety intervention: either escalating to a more conservative rule-based fallback planner or soliciting extended chain-of-thought reasoning with explicit risk quantification tokens. Calibration is performed on a held-out validation split from nuPlan/nuScenes, producing coverage guarantees (e.g., 90% marginal coverage) without retraining. The uncertainty scores also serve as auxiliary rewards in a second stage of GRPO fine-tuning, penalizing confident predictions in high-uncertainty regions. Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan closed-loop, CARLA adversarial scenarios, and out-of-distribution driving conditions (weather, rare maneuvers), measuring collision rate, intervention frequency, trajectory quality, and formal coverage validity compared to AutoVLA baseline and MC-dropout uncertainty baselines.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Scenario Augmentation for Robust Causal Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: Current VLA models like AutoVLA learn correlational patterns between visual scenes and driving actions, but lack genuine causal understanding of why certain actions are taken. This leads to brittle behavior when encountering spurious correlations (e.g., always braking near red objects regardless of context) and poor generalization to novel causal structures. Proposed Method: We introduce CausalVLA, which augments VLA training with counterfactual scenario generation and causal intervention objectives. Using a controllable neural scene renderer (NeRF-based), we systematically generate counterfactual variants of training scenes by intervening on causal factors: removing pedestrians, changing traffic light states, altering vehicle trajectories. For each real scenario, we create a counterfactual triplet (original scene, intervened scene, action delta), training the model to predict how actions should change under interventions via a contrastive causal loss. We additionally introduce a causal chain-of-thought prompt structure that explicitly asks the model to identify the primary causal factor driving each decision. The GRPO reinforcement fine-tuning is extended with a causal consistency reward penalizing action predictions that violate counterfactual invariances. Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA using novel causal robustness benchmarks measuring performance under distribution shifts of individual scene factors, comparing against AutoVLA and standard data augmentation baselines on both planning accuracy and causal consistency metrics.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Reasoning for Safety-Critical Scenario Generation and Robustness Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates strong average-case planning performance, its robustness in rare safety-critical scenarios (e.g., sudden pedestrian crossings, adversarial cut-ins) remains poorly understood. Standard benchmarks lack sufficient tail-event coverage, and existing augmentation methods cannot systematically probe causal failure modes of VLA models. Proposed Method: We introduce CausalVLA, a framework that leverages the chain-of-thought reasoning traces produced by slow-thinking VLA models to construct structured causal graphs of driving decisions. Using these graphs, we apply counterfactual interventions (e.g., 'what if the pedestrian appeared 2 seconds earlier?') to generate targeted adversarial scenarios via a diffusion-based scene editor conditioned on the causal graph modifications. We then use these counterfactual scenarios for both robustness evaluation and adversarial fine-tuning via GRPO with a safety-weighted reward that penalizes collision and near-miss events. Experiments: (1) Evaluate AutoVLA and CausalVLA on a new Counterfactual Safety Benchmark derived from nuPlan and CARLA with 500+ adversarial scenarios; (2) Measure collision rate reduction versus standard GRPO fine-tuning; (3) Ablate causal graph depth and intervention granularity; (4) Compare counterfactual augmentation against random perturbation baselines on closed-loop CARLA Route Completion and Infraction Score metrics.

title: SafetyGRPO: Constrained Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Safety-Critical Scenario Handling in Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:
Problem: While AutoVLA's GRPO-based reinforcement fine-tuning improves planning efficiency in routine scenarios, it lacks explicit mechanisms to ensure safety constraints (collision avoidance, traffic rule compliance) are maintained during RL optimization. Standard reward shaping may inadvertently trade safety for efficiency, particularly in rare but critical edge cases like pedestrian crossings, emergency vehicles, or adverse weather.

Proposed Method: We introduce SafetyGRPO, a constrained reinforcement fine-tuning framework that augments GRPO with a dual-objective optimization: (1) a primary efficiency reward mirroring AutoVLA's approach, and (2) hard safety constraints formulated as Lagrangian penalties that penalize policy updates violating predefined safety margins. We construct a curated safety-critical scenario bank from nuPlan and CARLA's adversarial environments. A safety classifier head trained on this bank dynamically triggers 'slow thinking' mode with mandatory chain-of-thought safety reasoning when scenario risk exceeds a threshold, preventing premature fast-thinking shortcuts in dangerous situations. The Lagrange multipliers adapt online based on constraint violation frequency.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan's reactive simulation, CARLA's adversarial benchmark (scenarios involving pedestrian jaywalking, cut-ins, sudden braking), and a newly constructed Safety-nuScenes split. Metrics include collision rate, traffic violation rate, planning efficiency score, and safety-efficiency Pareto frontier analysis compared to AutoVLA and baseline GRPO variants.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Conformal Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description: Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates strong planning performance, VLA models for autonomous driving lack principled uncertainty quantification. When the model is uncertain about its trajectory predictions, it should signal for human intervention or fallback to conservative behaviors—yet current VLA approaches provide no calibrated confidence estimates alongside their discrete action tokens. Proposed Method: We propose wrapping AutoVLA's tokenized trajectory outputs with conformal prediction sets that provide distribution-free, statistically guaranteed coverage of the true trajectory. Specifically, we (1) construct nonconformity scores from the autoregressive trajectory token probabilities using a calibration split, (2) generate prediction sets (multiple candidate trajectories) at a user-specified coverage level (e.g., 90%), and (3) introduce a risk-aware decision layer that triggers slow-thinking CoT reasoning when prediction set size exceeds a threshold, and requests handoff when sets remain large after re-reasoning. We additionally train a lightweight set-size predictor to anticipate uncertainty before full inference, enabling proactive mode switching. Planned Experiments: Evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA across scenario difficulty tiers, measuring (a) empirical coverage vs. nominal level, (b) average set size as an efficiency metric, (c) collision rate reduction when uncertainty-triggered handoffs are simulated, and (d) latency overhead vs. safety gain tradeoff compared to always-on slow thinking in AutoVLA.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Hallucination Detection and Safe Fallback for Vision-Language-Action Models in Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios
description: Problem: VLA models like AutoVLA can confidently produce plausible-sounding but physically unsafe trajectories in rare or adversarial scenarios (e.g., occluded pedestrians, sensor degradation, edge-case weather), with no intrinsic mechanism to recognize when their reasoning is unreliable and defer to safer alternatives. We fine-tune using a modified GRPO reward that penalizes both unsafe trajectories and false-safe overconfident outputs, creating an uncertainty-aware policy gradient signal. Planned Experiments: (1) Out-of-distribution scenario detection accuracy on nuPlan corner cases and synthetic adversarial perturbations; (2) Closed-loop safety metrics (collision rate, TTC violations) in CARLA under sensor noise and occlusion; (3) Calibration curves (ECE) comparing against MC-Dropout and ensemble baselines; (4) Human study evaluating explanation quality of uncertainty tokens in ambiguous driving scenes.

The VLA is then trained with contrastive chain-of-thought supervision: the model must explicitly reason about 'what would happen if X were different' before committing to a trajectory. A causal consistency reward is added to GRPO, penalizing action outputs that violate counterfactual invariance (i.e., actions that change when causally irrelevant factors are perturbed).

Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA safety-critical benchmarks, comparing collision rates and comfort metrics against AutoVLA and standard data augmentation baselines. title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Intervention Training for Causally Grounded Vision-Language-Action Driving Models

We add a causal consistency loss that enforces invariant action predictions under irrelevant interventions and sensitive action predictions under relevant ones. This loss is incorporated into the GRPO-style reinforcement fine-tuning loop using trajectory deviation as a reward signal. title: SafetyGRPO: Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for VLA Models via Multi-Objective Reward Shaping in Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios
description:
Problem: AutoVLA uses GRPO to improve planning efficiency, but its reward signal is primarily trajectory accuracy-focused. In safety-critical scenarios (pedestrian crossings, emergency vehicles, adverse weather), optimizing solely for trajectory quality can inadvertently reinforce behaviors that are efficient yet unsafe. Current VLA driving models lack principled safety constraint enforcement during RL fine-tuning.

Proposed Method: We extend the GRPO framework with a multi-objective constrained reward formulation (SafetyGRPO) that simultaneously optimizes: (1) trajectory accuracy reward, (2) a safety constraint reward derived from TTC (time-to-collision) and proximity violations, and (3) a comfort reward penalizing jerk/acceleration discontinuities. We introduce a Lagrangian relaxation mechanism to balance these objectives dynamically during training. Additionally, we curate a Safety-Critical Scenario Bank by mining rare but dangerous edge cases from nuPlan and Waymo datasets, using this targeted replay buffer to bias GRPO sampling toward high-stakes situations.

Experiments: We evaluate on CARLA's LeaderBoard 2.0 (infraction rate, route completion), nuPlan safety metrics, and a newly constructed adversarial pedestrian benchmark. Ablations compare single-reward GRPO vs. SafetyGRPO, analyze Lagrange multiplier dynamics, and measure reasoning verbosity reduction in routine vs. safety-critical scenarios. We hypothesize SafetyGRPO achieves 30%+ infraction reduction while maintaining competitive trajectory accuracy.

title: SafeVLA: Uncertainty-Aware Abstention and Fallback Triggering for Vision-Language-Action Driving Models
description:

Threshold calibration uses exchangeability-based conformal coverage guarantees on a validation split.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan closed-loop with injected adversarial perturbations (fog, occlusions, sensor dropout), measuring abstention recall on unsafe scenarios, false abstention rate on normal driving, and downstream collision rate when fallback is activated. Comparisons against standard AutoVLA, temperature scaling, and MC-Dropout baselines establish the safety-reliability tradeoff gains.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA with newly constructed counterfactual test sets measuring (1) causal sensitivity (action changes when causal factors change), (2) causal specificity (stability under non-causal perturbations), (3) standard closed-loop safety metrics, and (4) out-of-distribution generalization on rare edge cases, comparing against AutoVLA and data-augmentation baselines.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Intervention Training for Causally-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: Current VLA models like AutoVLA learn correlational patterns between visual scenes, language instructions, and trajectories, but fail to disentangle causal factors from spurious correlations (e.g., associating wet roads with slower speeds rather than understanding friction causality). This leads to brittle generalization under distribution shift and inability to explain 'why' a trajectory was chosen.

Proposed Method: CausalVLA augments the AutoVLA training framework with a counterfactual intervention module. During training, we systematically generate counterfactual scene variations using a diffusion-based image editor (e.g., removing pedestrians, changing weather, altering traffic signs) and train the model to produce consistent causal explanations for trajectory changes between original and counterfactual pairs. We introduce a causal consistency reward into the GRPO fine-tuning stage: the model is rewarded when its chain-of-thought reasoning correctly identifies which scene elements causally influenced trajectory decisions, verified against counterfactual trajectory differences. A structural causal model (SCM) serves as a lightweight supervising oracle trained on ground-truth intervention pairs.

Experiments: (1) OOD generalization on corrupted nuScenes/Waymo variants; (2) Counterfactual reasoning accuracy benchmarks measuring explanation fidelity; (3) CARLA closed-loop evaluation under novel weather/density conditions; (4) Ablation of causal vs. standard GRPO rewards; (5) Human evaluation of reasoning plausibility on edge cases.

title: SafetyGRPO: Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Safety-Critical Scenario Planning in Vision-Language-Action Models
description: Problem: AutoVLA's GRPO-based reinforcement fine-tuning optimizes for trajectory quality in typical driving scenarios but lacks explicit mechanisms to handle rare, safety-critical edge cases (e.g., pedestrian jaywalking, sudden obstacles, adversarial cut-ins). Standard reward signals averaging over scenario distributions may under-weight catastrophic but infrequent failures, leaving VLA models brittle in long-tail situations. Proposed Method: We introduce SafetyGRPO, a constrained policy optimization framework for VLA models that augments standard trajectory reward with a safety constraint layer. We construct a curated safety-critical dataset by mining hard scenarios from existing datasets (nuPlan, Waymo) and generating adversarial perturbations via simulation. Training introduces a dual-objective GRPO variant: a primary reward for trajectory accuracy and a Lagrangian penalty term for constraint violations (collision probability, time-to-collision thresholds, kinematic feasibility). We additionally propose a safety-aware thinking mode selector that triggers slow chain-of-thought reasoning specifically when safety-relevant scene elements are detected, rather than relying purely on scenario complexity heuristics. Experiments: We evaluate on CARLA safety challenge benchmarks, nuPlan reactive agents, and a novel adversarial split of Waymo. Metrics include infraction rate, comfort scores, and reasoning trigger precision/recall on safety-critical events. Ablations isolate contributions of the Lagrangian penalty and the safety-triggered reasoning selector.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Intervention Training for Causally-Grounded Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: Current VLA models like AutoVLA learn correlations between visual scenes and actions but may exploit spurious statistical regularities (e.g., always decelerating near pedestrian-colored pixels regardless of trajectory relevance). This leads to brittle behavior under distribution shift and prevents genuine causal understanding of why specific actions are chosen.

Proposed Method: We introduce CausalVLA, which augments VLA training with counterfactual intervention via a structured causal reasoning module. During training, we (1) apply targeted visual interventions—synthetically removing/replacing causal objects (other vehicles, pedestrians, traffic signs) using inpainting—and construct contrastive pairs requiring the model to produce different trajectories only when causally relevant objects change; (2) introduce a Counterfactual Consistency Loss that penalizes action changes under non-causal interventions (background texture, lighting) while rewarding sensitivity to causal ones; (3) extend GRPO rewards to include a causal fidelity score measuring whether the chain-of-thought reasoning correctly identifies which scene elements drove the action decision, verified against intervention ground truth.

Experiments: We evaluate on nuPlan and CARLA closed-loop benchmarks, adding a novel CausalRobustness evaluation suite with systematically constructed intervention scenarios. Ablations compare standard GRPO vs. causally-augmented GRPO, measuring L2 trajectory error, collision rate, and reasoning attribution accuracy under distribution shift conditions including adverse weather and novel actor configurations.

title: CausalVLA: Counterfactual Reasoning for Safety-Critical Scenario Discovery in Vision-Language-Action Autonomous Driving
description:
Problem: While AutoVLA demonstrates adaptive reasoning for typical driving scenarios, it lacks mechanisms to systematically identify and reason about safety-critical edge cases. Current VLA models trained on logged data are rarely exposed to near-miss or failure scenarios, leaving their causal understanding of accident-inducing conditions untested and underdeveloped.

Proposed Method: We introduce CausalVLA, which augments the VLA training pipeline with counterfactual scenario generation and causal intervention reasoning. Using a diffusion-based scene editor, we generate counterfactual visual observations by intervening on scene elements (e.g., occlusions, adversarial agent behaviors, weather perturbations) while preserving physical plausibility. We then train the VLA model with an additional counterfactual reasoning head that predicts 'what would have happened' under alternative actions, supervised by physics-based rollout outcomes. A contrastive GRPO reward explicitly penalizes failure to distinguish safe vs. unsafe counterfactual trajectories. This forces the model to internalize causal structure rather than correlational shortcuts.

Experiments: (1) Safety-critical closed-loop evaluation on CARLA adversarial scenarios and nuPlan reactive agents; (2) Ablation over counterfactual augmentation quantity and diversity; (3) Out-of-distribution generalization on Waymo interactive segments; (4) Human study comparing causal explanation quality against AutoVLA chain-of-thought baselines; (5) Collision rate reduction metrics across all benchmarks.

title: SafetyGRPO: Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Safety-Critical Scenario Planning in Vision-Language-Action Models
description: Problem: AutoVLA's GRPO-based reinforcement fine-tuning optimizes for planning efficiency and trajectory accuracy but lacks explicit safety constraint enforcement. In safety-critical scenarios (pedestrian crossings, emergency vehicles, adverse weather), the model may generate trajectories that minimize planning error while violating implicit safety rules not captured by trajectory-matching rewards. Proposed Method: We introduce SafetyGRPO, an extension of GRPO that incorporates a constrained policy optimization framework with dual reward signals: (1) the standard trajectory quality reward from AutoVLA, and (2) a safety violation penalty reward derived from a learned safety critic trained on labeled near-miss and collision scenarios from real-world dashcam data. We further add a 'safety slow-thinking trigger' — a lightweight binary classifier that forces chain-of-thought reasoning specifically when the safety critic detects high-risk contexts, overriding the fast-thinking mode. Experiments: We evaluate on (1) nuPlan's reactive agents benchmark focusing on collision rate and time-to-collision metrics, (2) CARLA Town05 Long with injected adversarial pedestrians, (3) a newly curated 'SafetyEdge' dataset of 500 dashcam clips with annotated near-miss events. Ablations compare standard GRPO vs. SafetyGRPO on the tradeoff between planning efficiency and safety violation rates across varying risk thresholds.
